paper_title: TARGET Benchmarking Table Retrieval for Generative Tasks
caption: Influence of corpus size on retrieval, illustrating the sensitivity in retrieval performance of dense retrievers when the corpus reaches a large scale.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The graph illustrates the relationship between the number of extra tables and the recall metric for two different retrieval methods.

The X-axis is labeled "# extra tables" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 40,000, with evenly spaced numerical labels at intervals of 20,000. The Y-axis is labeled "recall" and also has a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 0.6, with evenly spaced numerical labels at intervals of 0.2.

There are two lines on the graph, each representing a different retrieval method. The blue dashed line corresponds to "dense table embedding," while the orange dashed line represents "sparse lexical representation (tf-idf)". The blue line starts at approximately 0.75 on the Y-axis when the X-axis value is 0 and gradually decreases to around 0.5 as the X-axis value approaches 50,000. The orange line begins at roughly 0.1 on the Y-axis when the X-axis value is 0 and decreases to nearly 0 as the X-axis value reaches 50,000.

Both lines exhibit a downward trend as the number of extra tables increases, with no visible peaks or plateaus. The blue line consistently maintains higher recall values than the orange line across the entire range of the X-axis.
